claim: Regulation of the outer kinetochore complex Ndc80 is essential to ensure correct kinetochore-microtubule attachments during mitosis.
source: Regulation of the outer kinetochore complex Ndc80 is essential to ensure correct kinetochore-microtubule attachments during mitosis.
evidence: This is a general statement in the abstract that draws from established scientific consensus about the Ndc80 complex's role in mitosis.

claim: Tight bending of the Ndc80 complex inhibits its microtubule binding.
source: Here, we present a novel mechanism of regulation that is intrinsic to its structure; tight bending of the Ndc80 complex inhibits its microtubule binding.
evidence: This is a primary finding of the study supported by experimental data presented throughout the manuscript, including FRET measurements and microtubule binding assays.

claim: The Saccharomyces cerevisiae Ndc80 complex can fluctuate between straight and bent forms.
source: Using single molecule Förster resonance energy transfer (FRET), we show that the Saccharomyces cerevisiae Ndc80 complex can fluctuate between straight and bent forms, and that binding of the complex to microtubules selects for straightened forms.
evidence: This claim is supported by single molecule FRET data presented in the manuscript showing dynamic conformational changes.

claim: Binding of the Ndc80 complex to microtubules selects for straightened forms.
source: Using single molecule Förster resonance energy transfer (FRET), we show that the Saccharomyces cerevisiae Ndc80 complex can fluctuate between straight and bent forms, and that binding of the complex to microtubules selects for straightened forms.
evidence: This is supported by FRET measurements showing lower FRET efficiency for microtubule-bound Ndc80 complexes compared to free complexes.

claim: The loop region of the Ndc80 complex enables its bent conformation.
source: The loop region of the complex enables its bent conformation, as deletion of the loop promotes straightening.
evidence: This is supported by experimental data showing that deletion of part of the loop (Δ490-510) reduces high-FRET values.

claim: Deletion of the loop promotes straightening of the Ndc80 complex.
source: The loop region of the complex enables its bent conformation, as deletion of the loop promotes straightening.
evidence: This is supported by FRET data showing that Ndc80 Δ490-510 exhibits only 5.6% high-FRET values compared to 25% for wild-type.

claim: The kinetochore complex MIND enhances microtubule binding by opposing the tightly bent, auto-inhibited conformation of the Ndc80 complex.
source: In addition, the kinetochore complex MIND enhances microtubule binding by opposing the tightly bent, auto-inhibited conformation of the Ndc80 complex.
evidence: This is supported by FRET data showing that Ndc80-MIND co-complexes exhibit only 4.9% high-FRET values and by residence time measurements showing increased microtubule binding.

claim: Prior to its assembly at the kinetochore, the Ndc80 complex interchanges between bent (auto-inhibited) and open conformations.
source: We suggest that prior to its assembly at the kinetochore, the Ndc80 complex interchanges between bent (auto-inhibited) and open conformations.
evidence: This is a speculative interpretation based on the FRET data showing dynamic conformational changes.

claim: Once assembled at the kinetochore, association of the Ndc80 complex with MIND stabilizes it in a straightened form for higher affinity microtubule binding.
source: Once assembled, its association with MIND stabilizes the Ndc80 complex in a straightened form for higher affinity microtubule binding.
evidence: This is supported by FRET data showing low FRET for Ndc80-MIND co-complexes and residence time data showing enhanced microtubule binding.

claim: The Ndc80 complex is directly involved in kinetochore-microtubule attachment.
source: It is directly involved in kinetochore-microtubule attachment, in bearing mechanical load at the kinetochore-microtubule interface, and in correction of erroneous attachments (Powers et al., 2009; Umbreit et al., 2012; Etemad et al., 2015).
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to previous studies.

claim: The Ndc80 complex is involved in bearing mechanical load at the kinetochore-microtubule interface.
source: It is directly involved in kinetochore-microtubule attachment, in bearing mechanical load at the kinetochore-microtubule interface, and in correction of erroneous attachments (Powers et al., 2009; Umbreit et al., 2012; Etemad et al., 2015).
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to previous studies.

claim: The Ndc80 complex is involved in correction of erroneous kinetochore-microtubule attachments.
source: It is directly involved in kinetochore-microtubule attachment, in bearing mechanical load at the kinetochore-microtubule interface, and in correction of erroneous attachments (Powers et al., 2009; Umbreit et al., 2012; Etemad et al., 2015).
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to previous studies.

claim: The Ndc80 complex specifically localizes only to kinetochores and binds the plus-ends of microtubules in vivo.
source: The Ndc80 complex specifically localizes only to kinetochores and binds the plus-ends of microtubules in vivo.
evidence: This is a statement about the known localization pattern of Ndc80 in cells, drawing from established knowledge.

claim: Even in instances of Ndc80 overexpression in yeast or mammalian cells, excess Ndc80 is not found along the microtubule lattice in the mitotic spindle.
source: Even in instances of Ndc80 overexpression in yeast or mammalian cells, excess Ndc80 is not found along the microtubule lattice in the mitotic spindle (Tang and Toda, 2015; Diaz-Rodríguez et al., 2008).
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to previous studies.

claim: The Ndc80 complex is an elongated and flexible heterotetramer.
source: The Ndc80 complex is an elongated and flexible heterotetramer, with two globular ends connected by a coiled coil, which displays a variety of conformations in negative stain electron micrographs (Wang et al., 2008; Zhang et al., 2012) and in crystallized forms (Ciferri et al., 2008; Valverde et al., 2016).
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to previous structural studies.

claim: The Ndc80 complex has two globular ends connected by a coiled coil.
source: The Ndc80 complex is an elongated and flexible heterotetramer, with two globular ends connected by a coiled coil, which displays a variety of conformations in negative stain electron micrographs (Wang et al., 2008; Zhang et al., 2012) and in crystallized forms (Ciferri et al., 2008; Valverde et al., 2016).
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to previous structural studies.

claim: The Ndc80 complex displays a variety of conformations in negative stain electron micrographs.
source: The Ndc80 complex is an elongated and flexible heterotetramer, with two globular ends connected by a coiled coil, which displays a variety of conformations in negative stain electron micrographs (Wang et al., 2008; Zhang et al., 2012) and in crystallized forms (Ciferri et al., 2008; Valverde et al., 2016).
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to previous structural studies.

claim: The Ndc80 complex displays a variety of conformations in crystallized forms.
source: The Ndc80 complex is an elongated and flexible heterotetramer, with two globular ends connected by a coiled coil, which displays a variety of conformations in negative stain electron micrographs (Wang et al., 2008; Zhang et al., 2012) and in crystallized forms (Ciferri et al., 2008; Valverde et al., 2016).
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to previous structural studies.

claim: The flexibility of the Ndc80 complex is important in vivo.
source: Studies suggest that its flexibility is important in vivo (Wang et al., 2008; Maure et al., 2011; Joglekar et al., 2009; Tien et al., 2014).
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to previous studies.

claim: The ability of the Ndc80 complex to adopt both straightened and bent conformations is necessary for the proper progression of mitosis.
source: For example, the ability of the Ndc80 complex to adopt both straightened and bent conformations is necessary for the proper progression of mitosis and implicated in the resolution of aberrant kinetochore-microtubule attachments (Tien et al., 2014).
evidence: This claim is supported by citation to a previous study.

claim: The ability of the Ndc80 complex to adopt both straightened and bent conformations is implicated in the resolution of aberrant kinetochore-microtubule attachments.
source: For example, the ability of the Ndc80 complex to adopt both straightened and bent conformations is necessary for the proper progression of mitosis and implicated in the resolution of aberrant kinetochore-microtubule attachments (Tien et al., 2014).
evidence: This claim is supported by citation to a previous study.

claim: Cross-linking data suggest that the Ndc80 complex has the capacity to adopt a tightly bent conformation.
source: Cross-linking data suggest that this flexibility is extreme in its range: the Ndc80 complex not only bends, but also has the capacity to adopt a tightly bent conformation (Tien et al., 2014).
evidence: This claim is supported by citation to a previous study.

claim: Several studies have suggested that microtubule binding by the Ndc80 complex is auto-inhibited.
source: Several studies have suggested that microtubule binding by the Ndc80 complex is auto-inhibited (Cheeseman et al., 2006; Kudalkar et al., 2015).
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to previous studies.

claim: The MIND/Mtw1 complex bridges the inner and outer layers of the kinetochore.
source: The MIND/Mtw1 complex bridges the inner and outer layers of the kinetochore, directly binding the Ndc80 complex and tethering it to the DNA-binding kinetochore components (Maskell et al., 2010).
evidence: This claim is supported by citation to a previous study.

claim: The MIND complex directly binds the Ndc80 complex.
source: The MIND/Mtw1 complex bridges the inner and outer layers of the kinetochore, directly binding the Ndc80 complex and tethering it to the DNA-binding kinetochore components (Maskell et al., 2010).
evidence: This claim is supported by citation to a previous study.

claim: The MIND complex tethers the Ndc80 complex to the DNA-binding kinetochore components.
source: The MIND/Mtw1 complex bridges the inner and outer layers of the kinetochore, directly binding the Ndc80 complex and tethering it to the DNA-binding kinetochore components (Maskell et al., 2010).
evidence: This claim is supported by citation to a previous study.

claim: In vitro, the addition of MIND to the Ndc80 complex increases its residence time on the microtubule lattice by nearly fourfold.
source: In vitro, the addition of MIND to the Ndc80 complex increases its residence time on the microtubule lattice by nearly fourfold (Kudalkar et al., 2015).
evidence: This claim is supported by citation to a previous study.

claim: Individual full-length Ndc80 complexes bound transiently and relatively weakly to microtubules, with a mean residence time of 2.9 ± 0.3 s.
source: Consistent with previous studies (Kudalkar et al., 2015; Powers et al., 2009), individual full-length Ndc80 complexes bound transiently and relatively weakly to microtubules, with a mean residence time of 2.9 ± 0.3 s (Figure 1B and C).
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 1B and C, and is consistent with previous studies.

claim: Individual Broccoli-GFP dimers bound to microtubules with a mean residence time of 5.6 ± 0.7 s.
source: Individual Broccoli-GFP dimers bound longer, with a mean residence time of 5.6 ± 0.7 s, roughly twice as long as full-length tetrameric Ndc80-GFP, suggesting that removal of the Spc24/Spc25 end of the complex relieves an auto-inhibitory effect (Figure 1B and C).
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 1B and C.

claim: The mean residence time of Broccoli-GFP on microtubules is roughly twice as long as full-length tetrameric Ndc80-GFP.
source: Individual Broccoli-GFP dimers bound longer, with a mean residence time of 5.6 ± 0.7 s, roughly twice as long as full-length tetrameric Ndc80-GFP, suggesting that removal of the Spc24/Spc25 end of the complex relieves an auto-inhibitory effect (Figure 1B and C).
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 1B and C.

claim: Removal of the Spc24/Spc25 end of the Ndc80 complex relieves an auto-inhibitory effect.
source: Individual Broccoli-GFP dimers bound longer, with a mean residence time of 5.6 ± 0.7 s, roughly twice as long as full-length tetrameric Ndc80-GFP, suggesting that removal of the Spc24/Spc25 end of the complex relieves an auto-inhibitory effect (Figure 1B and C).
evidence: This is an inference based on the comparison of residence times between Broccoli and full-length Ndc80.

claim: When free Spc24/Spc25 dimer was added in sixtyfold excess to Broccoli-GFP, the mean residence time of Broccoli-GFP on microtubules was reduced to 3.3 ± 0.4 s.
source: Indeed, when free Spc24/Spc25 dimer was purified (Figure 1—figure supplement 1C) and added in sixtyfold excess to Broccoli-GFP, the mean residence time of Broccoli-GFP on microtubules was reduced to 3.3 ± 0.4 s, which is statistically indistinguishable (p=0.4) from the residence time of full-length Ndc80 complex alone.
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data.

claim: The mean residence time of Broccoli-GFP with sixtyfold excess Spc24/Spc25 (3.3 ± 0.4 s) is statistically indistinguishable (p=0.4) from the residence time of full-length Ndc80 complex alone.
source: Indeed, when free Spc24/Spc25 dimer was purified (Figure 1—figure supplement 1C) and added in sixtyfold excess to Broccoli-GFP, the mean residence time of Broccoli-GFP on microtubules was reduced to 3.3 ± 0.4 s, which is statistically indistinguishable (p=0.4) from the residence time of full-length Ndc80 complex alone.
evidence: This claim is supported by statistical analysis of experimental data.

claim: Adding MIND-GFP to full-length Ndc80 complex increased its residence time on microtubules more than threefold, from 2.9 ± 0.3 s to 9.8 ± 1.1 s.
source: Adding MIND-GFP to full-length Ndc80 complex increased its residence time on microtubules more than threefold, from 2.9 ± 0.3 s to 9.8 ± 1.1 s (Figure 1B and C), consistent with previous measurements (Kudalkar et al., 2015).
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 1B and C, and is consistent with previous measurements.

claim: Addition of a tenfold excess of Spc24/Spc25 dimer brought the residence time for the Ndc80-MIND-GFP co-complex down to 4.1 ± 0.5 s.
source: This MIND-dependent increase was almost completely abolished by addition of a tenfold excess of Spc24/Spc25 dimer, which brought the residence time for the Ndc80-MIND-GFP co-complex down to 4.1 ± 0.5 s (Figure 1B and C), similar to that of full-length tetrameric Ndc80 alone.
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 1B and C.

claim: A mutant Spc24/Spc25 dimer that is unable to associate with MIND, when added in tenfold excess, sharply reduced the residence time of the Ndc80-MIND-GFP co-complex, down to 4.2 ± 0.5 s.
source: Likewise, a mutant Spc24/Spc25 dimer that is unable to associate with MIND (Malvezzi et al., 2013), when added in tenfold excess, also sharply reduced the residence time of the Ndc80-MIND-GFP co-complex, down to 4.2 ± 0.5 s (Figure 1—figure supplement 3).
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 1—figure supplement 3.

claim: The excess Spc24/Spc25 dimer interacts directly with the Ndc80 complex for inhibition, rather than competing away MIND.
source: This observation indicates that the excess Spc24/Spc25 dimer interacts directly with the Ndc80 complex for inhibition, rather than competing away MIND.
evidence: This is an inference based on the observation that a mutant Spc24/Spc25 unable to bind MIND still inhibits the Ndc80-MIND co-complex.

claim: Free Spc24/Spc25 dimer does not detectably bind microtubules by itself.
source: Free Spc24/Spc25 dimer does not detectably bind microtubules by itself (Wei et al., 2007).
evidence: This claim is supported by citation to a previous study.

claim: The Spc24/Spc25 dimer can interact with Ndc80/Nuf2 independently of the tetramerization domain.
source: Altogether, our observations show that the Spc24/Spc25 dimer can interact with Ndc80/Nuf2 independently of the tetramerization domain, and that this secondary interaction is sufficient to inhibit the microtubule binding of Ndc80/Nuf2, of the full-length Ndc80 complex, and of the MIND-Ndc80 co-complex.
evidence: This is an inference based on the experimental observations showing that free Spc24/Spc25 can inhibit Broccoli and Ndc80-MIND.

claim: The secondary interaction between Spc24/Spc25 and Ndc80/Nuf2 is sufficient to inhibit the microtubule binding of Ndc80/Nuf2.
source: Altogether, our observations show that the Spc24/Spc25 dimer can interact with Ndc80/Nuf2 independently of the tetramerization domain, and that this secondary interaction is sufficient to inhibit the microtubule binding of Ndc80/Nuf2, of the full-length Ndc80 complex, and of the MIND-Ndc80 co-complex.
evidence: This is an inference based on the experimental observations.

claim: The secondary interaction between Spc24/Spc25 and Ndc80/Nuf2 is sufficient to inhibit the microtubule binding of the full-length Ndc80 complex.
source: Altogether, our observations show that the Spc24/Spc25 dimer can interact with Ndc80/Nuf2 independently of the tetramerization domain, and that this secondary interaction is sufficient to inhibit the microtubule binding of Ndc80/Nuf2, of the full-length Ndc80 complex, and of the MIND-Ndc80 co-complex.
evidence: This is an inference based on the experimental observations.

claim: The secondary interaction between Spc24/Spc25 and Ndc80/Nuf2 is sufficient to inhibit the microtubule binding of the MIND-Ndc80 co-complex.
source: Altogether, our observations show that the Spc24/Spc25 dimer can interact with Ndc80/Nuf2 independently of the tetramerization domain, and that this secondary interaction is sufficient to inhibit the microtubule binding of Ndc80/Nuf2, of the full-length Ndc80 complex, and of the MIND-Ndc80 co-complex.
evidence: This is an inference based on the experimental observations.

claim: Electrostatic interactions are crucial for binding of the Ndc80 complex to microtubules.
source: Electrostatic interactions are crucial for binding of the Ndc80 complex to microtubules.
evidence: This is a statement drawing from established knowledge about Ndc80-microtubule interactions.

claim: Basic residues located on the globular (calponin homology) domains of the Ndc80 and Nuf2 subunits interact with acidic patches on the surface of the microtubule to enable microtubule binding.
source: Basic residues located on the globular (calponin homology) domains of the Ndc80 and Nuf2 subunits have been shown to interact with acidic patches on the surface of the microtubule to enable microtubule binding (Ciferri et al., 2008).
evidence: This claim is supported by citation to a previous study.

claim: Charge-charge interactions between the N-terminal 'tail' of Ndc80 and the microtubule lattice tune microtubule binding through phosphorylation.
source: Additionally, charge-charge interactions between the N-terminal 'tail' of Ndc80 and the microtubule lattice tune this microtubule binding through phosphorylation (Zaytsev et al., 2015; Zaytsev et al., 2014).
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to previous studies.

claim: Three acidic residues located on one face of the Spc25 subunit are highly conserved.
source: Sequence alignment revealed three acidic residues located on one face of the Spc25 subunit that are highly conserved, suggesting functional importance (Figure 1—figure supplement 1E).
evidence: This claim is supported by sequence alignment data shown in Figure 1—figure supplement 1E.

claim: When added in sixtyfold excess, Spc24/Spc25-7K failed to detectably inhibit the microtubule-binding activity of Broccoli-GFP (mean residence time of 6.9 ± 0.6 s with versus 5.6 ± 0.7 s without the addition Spc24/Spc25-7K; p=0.16).
source: When added in sixtyfold excess, Spc24/Spc25-7K failed to detectably inhibit the microtubule-binding activity of Broccoli-GFP (mean residence time of 6.9 ± 0.6 s with versus 5.6 ± 0.7 s without the addition Spc24/Spc25-7K; p=0.16), in contrast to the wild-type Spc24/Spc25 dimer (3.3 ± 0.4 s with versus 5.6 ± 0.7 s without; p=0.006) (Figure 1B and C).
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 1B and C.

claim: Electrostatic interactions play an important role in auto-inhibition of the Ndc80 complex.
source: While a full-length, tetrameric Ndc80 complex carrying the 7K charge-reversal mutations could not be purified (see Materials and methods), the normal microtubule-binding activity of the Ndc80 complex in the presence of a large excess of Spc24/Spc25-7K dimer nevertheless suggests that electrostatic interactions play an important role in auto-inhibition of the complex.
evidence: This is an inference based on the observation that charge-reversal mutations in Spc24/Spc25 abolish its inhibitory effect.

claim: Electron micrographs of purified, negatively stained samples of Ndc80 complex show that the coiled-coil can adopt a variety of conformations, with a tendency to bend at or near the 'loop.'
source: Electron micrographs of purified, negatively stained samples of Ndc80 complex show that the coiled-coil can adopt a variety of conformations, with a tendency to bend at or near the 'loop,' an unstructured region of 50–60 residues within the Ndc80 protein (Wang et al., 2008; Zhang et al., 2012).
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to previous studies.

claim: The loop is an unstructured region of 50–60 residues within the Ndc80 protein.
source: Electron micrographs of purified, negatively stained samples of Ndc80 complex show that the coiled-coil can adopt a variety of conformations, with a tendency to bend at or near the 'loop,' an unstructured region of 50–60 residues within the Ndc80 protein (Wang et al., 2008; Zhang et al., 2012).
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to previous studies.

claim: Genetic evidence suggests the Ndc80 complex must bend tightly to function properly in vivo.
source: Genetic evidence suggests the complex must bend tightly to function properly in vivo (Tien et al., 2014), but the propensity of the complex for tight bending has not been directly examined.
evidence: This claim is supported by citation to a previous study.

claim: The end-labeled Ndc80 complex exhibited a FRET efficiency of 0.29.
source: The end-labeled Ndc80 complex exhibited a FRET efficiency of 0.29 (Figure 2E), a value intermediate between the positive and negative controls (0.53 and 0.10, respectively).
evidence: This claim is supported by bulk FRET measurement data shown in Figure 2E.

claim: In solution, the Ndc80 complex can adopt a tightly bent conformation, which brings its two ends into close proximity.
source: This observation indicates that in solution, the Ndc80 complex can adopt a tightly bent conformation, which brings its two ends into close proximity.
evidence: This is an inference based on the bulk FRET measurement showing intermediate FRET efficiency.

claim: Donor and acceptor signals recorded from individual end-labeled Ndc80 complexes were anti-correlated.
source: Donor and acceptor signals recorded from individual end-labeled Ndc80 complexes were anti-correlated; their FRET levels fluctuated between low values around zero and higher values approaching unity (Figure 3C).
evidence: This claim is supported by single molecule FRET data shown in Figure 3C.

claim: FRET levels from individual end-labeled Ndc80 complexes fluctuated between low values around zero and higher values approaching unity.
source: Donor and acceptor signals recorded from individual end-labeled Ndc80 complexes were anti-correlated; their FRET levels fluctuated between low values around zero and higher values approaching unity (Figure 3C).
evidence: This claim is supported by single molecule FRET data shown in Figure 3C.

claim: The distribution of FRET levels from end-labeled Ndc80 complexes was broad, with a large fraction (25%) of high-FRET values more than two standard deviations above the mean of the no-FRET population.
source: The distribution of FRET levels was broad, with a large fraction (25%) of high-FRET values more than two standard deviations above the mean of the no-FRET population (Figure 3E).
evidence: This claim is supported by single molecule FRET data shown in Figure 3E.

claim: Switching of the end-labeled Ndc80 complexes from low to high FRET occurred at a rate of kclosing = 0.23 ± 0.024 s−1.
source: Based on a simple two-state threshold-crossing analysis, switching of the end-labeled Ndc80 complexes from low to high FRET occurred at a rate of kclosing = 0.23 ± 0.024 s−1.
evidence: This claim is supported by analysis of single molecule FRET data.

claim: Switching of the end-labeled Ndc80 complexes from high to low FRET occurred at a rate of kopening = 0.96 ± 0.094 s−1.
source: Switching from high to low FRET was about fourfold faster, occurring at a rate of kopening = 0.96 ± 0.094 s−1 (Figure 3D).
evidence: This claim is supported by analysis of single molecule FRET data shown in Figure 3D.

claim: The high-FRET fluctuations were eliminated when intra-complex interactions were competitively inhibited by adding a hundredfold excess of free Spc24/Spc25.
source: The high-FRET fluctuations were eliminated when intra-complex interactions were competitively inhibited by adding a hundredfold excess of free Spc24/Spc25 (Figure 3F and G).
evidence: This claim is supported by single molecule FRET data shown in Figure 3F and G.

claim: The Ndc80 complex fluctuates dynamically between tightly bent and more open conformations.
source: Altogether, these single molecule observations confirm that the Ndc80 complex can adopt a tightly bent conformation, with both ends interacting closely together, in agreement with our bulk measurements, and they show that the complex fluctuates dynamically between tightly bent and more open conformations.
evidence: This is a conclusion based on the single molecule FRET data showing dynamic fluctuations.

claim: A flexible region of 50–60 residues within the Ndc80 protein interrupts the coiled-coil of Ndc80/Nuf2 to form a loop.
source: A flexible region of 50–60 residues within the Ndc80 protein interrupts the coiled-coil of Ndc80/Nuf2 to form a loop (Ciferri et al., 2005), which has been implicated in flexibility of the Ndc80 complex (Wang et al., 2008) and might serve as a binding site for other proteins (Maure et al., 2011).
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to previous studies.

claim: The loop has been implicated in flexibility of the Ndc80 complex.
source: A flexible region of 50–60 residues within the Ndc80 protein interrupts the coiled-coil of Ndc80/Nuf2 to form a loop (Ciferri et al., 2005), which has been implicated in flexibility of the Ndc80 complex (Wang et al., 2008) and might serve as a binding site for other proteins (Maure et al., 2011).
evidence: This claim is supported by citation to a previous study.

claim: The loop might serve as a binding site for other proteins.
source: A flexible region of 50–60 residues within the Ndc80 protein interrupts the coiled-coil of Ndc80/Nuf2 to form a loop (Ciferri et al., 2005), which has been implicated in flexibility of the Ndc80 complex (Wang et al., 2008) and might serve as a binding site for other proteins (Maure et al., 2011).
evidence: This is a speculative statement supported by citation to a previous study.

claim: In budding yeast cells, partial loop deletion (Ndc80 ∆490–510) confers temperature sensitivity.
source: In budding yeast cells, this partial loop deletion confers temperature sensitivity (Maure et al., 2011), indicating functional importance.
evidence: This claim is supported by citation to a previous study.

claim: The percentage of high-FRET values for Ndc80 ∆490–510 complexes was only 5.6%, which is fourfold less than the percentage measured from wild-type complexes.
source: FRET levels from purified individual Ndc80 ∆490–510 complexes were relatively low. The percentage of high-FRET values was only 5.6%, which is fourfold less than the percentage measured from wild-type complexes (Figure 4C and D), indicative of a more open form of the Ndc80 complex.
evidence: This claim is supported by single molecule FRET data shown in Figure 4C and D.

claim: Ndc80 ∆490–510 exhibited a longer residence time on microtubules than full-length wild type complex (3.1 ± 0.3 s vs. 2.1 ± 0.3 s).
source: Indeed, Ndc80 ∆490–510 exhibited a longer residence time on microtubules than full-length wild type complex (3.1 ± 0.3 s vs. 2.1 ± 0.3 s; Figure 4E and F).
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 4E and F.

claim: The loop region contributes to tight bending of the Ndc80 complex.
source: These observations confirm that the loop region contributes to tight bending of the Ndc80 complex and suggest that flexibility of the complex directly influences its microtubule binding.
evidence: This is a conclusion based on the FRET and residence time data for the loop deletion mutant.

claim: Flexibility of the Ndc80 complex directly influences its microtubule binding.
source: These observations confirm that the loop region contributes to tight bending of the Ndc80 complex and suggest that flexibility of the complex directly influences its microtubule binding.
evidence: This is an inference based on the correlation between reduced bending (in the loop deletion mutant) and increased microtubule binding.

claim: FRET from microtubule-bound Ndc80 complexes was low, with only a small fraction of high-FRET values, 6.2%.
source: As expected, FRET from the microtubule-bound complexes was low, with only a small fraction of high-FRET values, 6.2% (Figure 5B and D).
evidence: This claim is supported by single molecule FRET data shown in Figure 5B and D.

claim: The tightly bent conformation of the Ndc80 complex has a sixfold lower affinity for microtubules than the open conformation.
source: Assuming a simple four-state equilibrium between closed and open configurations (Figure 5E), the high-FRET fractions measured for microtubule-attached (Figure 5D) and 'free' Ndc80 complexes (coverslip-tethered, Figures 3D, 4C and 5D) imply that the tightly bent conformation has a sixfold lower affinity for microtubules than the open conformation (see Materials and methods).
evidence: This is a calculation based on the FRET data and a four-state equilibrium model.

claim: Association of the Ndc80 and MIND complexes together creates a co-complex with enhanced affinity for microtubules relative to Ndc80 complex alone.
source: Association of the Ndc80 and MIND complexes together creates a co-complex with enhanced affinity for microtubules relative to Ndc80 complex alone (Kudalkar et al., 2015).
evidence: This claim is supported by citation to a previous study.

claim: Genetic evidence suggests that MIND might prevent the Ndc80 complex from adopting the tightly bent, auto-inhibited state.
source: Genetic evidence suggests this enhancement might occur because MIND prevents the Ndc80 complex from adopting the tightly bent, auto-inhibited state (Tien et al., 2014; Kudalkar et al., 2015).
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to previous studies.

claim: The Ndc80 complex of C. elegans might be activated by the Mis12 complex, which is the worm counterpart of MIND.
source: The Ndc80 complex of C. elegans might also be activated by the Mis12 complex, which is the worm counterpart of MIND (Cheeseman et al., 2006).
evidence: This is a speculative statement supported by citation to a previous study.

claim: With a tenfold excess of free GFP-MIND, 33% of the end-labeled Ndc80 complexes formed co-complexes with MIND.
source: With a tenfold excess of free GFP-MIND, 33% of the end-labeled Ndc80 complexes formed co-complexes with MIND.
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental observation using three-color TIRF microscopy.

claim: FRET levels from Ndc80-MIND co-complexes were low, with only 4.9% of values significantly above the no-FRET population.
source: FRET levels from these Ndc80-MIND co-complexes were low, with only 4.9% of values significantly above the no-FRET population (Figure 5B and D).
evidence: This claim is supported by single molecule FRET data shown in Figure 5B and D.

claim: Association of the Ndc80 complex with MIND inhibits tight bending of the Ndc80 complex.
source: These observations show that association of the Ndc80 complex with MIND inhibits tight bending of the Ndc80 complex.
evidence: This is a conclusion based on the FRET data showing low FRET for Ndc80-MIND co-complexes.

claim: Tight bending of the Ndc80 complex leads to an auto-inhibited state that decreases microtubule affinity.
source: Using single molecule techniques, we found that the isolated Ndc80 complex fluctuates dynamically around its hinge region, adopting both open and closed conformations. Tight bending leads to an auto-inhibited state that decreases microtubule affinity.
evidence: This is a primary conclusion of the study supported by FRET and microtubule binding data.

claim: MIND-binding relieves auto-inhibition of the Ndc80 complex.
source: MIND-binding relieves this auto-inhibition, which explains how MIND enhances binding of the Ndc80 complex to microtubules.
evidence: This is a conclusion based on the FRET and residence time data showing that MIND prevents tight bending and increases microtubule binding.

claim: Deleting part of the loop region from yeast Ndc80 causes temperature-sensitive cell growth.
source: Deleting part of the loop region from yeast Ndc80 causes temperature-sensitive cell growth and frequent failures in the biorientation of sister kinetochores (Maure et al., 2011).
evidence: This claim is supported by citation to a previous study.

claim: Deleting part of the loop region from yeast Ndc80 causes frequent failures in the biorientation of sister kinetochores.
source: Deleting part of the loop region from yeast Ndc80 causes temperature-sensitive cell growth and frequent failures in the biorientation of sister kinetochores (Maure et al., 2011).
evidence: This claim is supported by citation to a previous study.

claim: A pair of point mutations near the loop region of Ndc80 causes temperature-sensitive growth and defects in biorientation.
source: Likewise, a pair of point mutations near the loop region of Ndc80 causes temperature-sensitive growth and defects in biorientation (Tien et al., 2014).
evidence: This claim is supported by citation to a previous study.

claim: Defects caused by loop-proximal point mutations in vivo were suppressed by additional cis-acting mutations in either Ndc80 or Nuf2 made on the opposite side of the loop region.
source: These defects in vivo were suppressed by additional cis-acting mutations, in either Ndc80 or Nuf2, made on exactly the opposite side of the loop region, suggesting that they interfere with tight bending of the Ndc80 complex (Tien et al., 2014).
evidence: This claim is supported by citation to a previous study.

claim: Loop-proximal point mutations enhance microtubule-binding of the Ndc80 complex in vitro, in a manner that mimics the addition of MIND.
source: Moreover, the same loop-proximal point mutations enhance microtubule-binding of the Ndc80 complex in vitro, in a manner that mimics the addition of MIND (Kudalkar et al., 2015).
evidence: This claim is supported by citation to a previous study.

claim: Tight bending of the Ndc80 complex might be required for proper regulation of kinetochore-microtubule attachments in vivo.
source: Based on our new findings, all these prior observations could have a single mechanistic basis: Tight bending of the Ndc80 complex might be required for proper regulation of kinetochore-microtubule attachments in vivo.
evidence: This is a speculative interpretation that integrates the current findings with previous observations.

claim: MIND interacts with a region of the Ndc80 complex far away from the microtubule-binding domains.
source: We established that MIND opposes the tightly bent form of the Ndc80 complex, but precisely how this translates to increased microtubule binding is less clear, given that MIND interacts with a region far away from the microtubule-binding domains of the Ndc80 complex.
evidence: This is a statement based on established knowledge of the Ndc80 complex structure and MIND binding site.

claim: The mechanism of MIND-mediated enhancement might be similar to the auto-inhibition of kinesin-1.
source: One possibility is that the mechanism is similar to the auto-inhibition of kinesin-1: kinesin-1 bends around its loop to bring its tail in close proximity to its heads, thereby inhibiting motor activity of the heads (Kaan et al., 2011).
evidence: This is a speculative comparison to another protein system, supported by citation.

claim: Kinesin-1 bends around its loop to bring its tail in close proximity to its heads, thereby inhibiting motor activity of the heads.
source: One possibility is that the mechanism is similar to the auto-inhibition of kinesin-1: kinesin-1 bends around its loop to bring its tail in close proximity to its heads, thereby inhibiting motor activity of the heads (Kaan et al., 2011).
evidence: This claim is supported by citation to a previous study on kinesin-1.

claim: Binding of the kinesin-1 tail to cargo blocks its interaction with the heads, thereby relieving auto-inhibition and enabling processive motility.
source: Binding of the kinesin-1 tail to cargo blocks its interaction with the heads, thereby relieving auto-inhibition and enabling processive motility.
evidence: This is a statement about the kinesin-1 mechanism, drawing from established knowledge.

claim: MIND binding to one end of the Ndc80 complex could block its interaction with the other end.
source: Like the cargo of kinesin-1, MIND binding to one end of the Ndc80 complex could simply block its interaction with the other end.
evidence: This is a speculative mechanism proposed by analogy to kinesin-1.

claim: The Ndc80-MIND co-complex has a residence time roughly twofold higher than Broccoli.
source: However, our data suggest that MIND may be doing more than simply relieving auto-inhibition: while the Broccoli construct (which lacks the Spc24/Spc25 dimer and is not auto-inhibited) resides on the microtubule lattice longer than the full-length Ndc80 complex, the Ndc80-MIND co-complex has a residence time still roughly twofold higher than Broccoli.
evidence: This is an inference based on comparison of residence time data.

claim: MIND might propagate a specific molecular reorganization to the Ndc80/Nuf2 end, through the coiled coil, to establish some preferred arrangement for microtubule binding.
source: This additional enhancement suggests that MIND might propagate a specific molecular reorganization to the Ndc80/Nuf2 end, through the coiled coil, to establish some preferred arrangement for microtubule binding.
evidence: This is a speculative mechanism proposed to explain the enhanced microtubule binding of Ndc80-MIND beyond simple relief of auto-inhibition.

claim: Allosteric communication through a coiled-coil has been seen in dynein.
source: Allosteric communication through a coiled-coil has been seen, for example, in dynein (Carter et al., 2008).
evidence: This claim is supported by citation to a previous study on dynein.

claim: The Ndc80 complex is flexible due to its internal loop region.
source: Previous literature determined that the Ndc80 complex is flexible (Wang et al., 2008) due to its internal loop region (Zhang et al., 2012) and can exist in both a bent and more open state (Tien et al., 2014).
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to previous studies.

claim: The Ndc80 complex can exist in both a bent and more open state.
source: Previous literature determined that the Ndc80 complex is flexible (Wang et al., 2008) due to its internal loop region (Zhang et al., 2012) and can exist in both a bent and more open state (Tien et al., 2014).
evidence: This claim is supported by citation to a previous study.

claim: The Ndc80 complex can readily adopt an extremely bent state, in which the two ends of the complex come within a few nanometers of each other.
source: Our data now show that it can readily adopt an extremely bent state, in which the two ends of the complex come within a few nanometers of each other, and that the loop region is required for this tight bending.
evidence: This is a conclusion based on the FRET data showing high-FRET values.

claim: The loop region is required for tight bending of the Ndc80 complex.
source: Our data now show that it can readily adopt an extremely bent state, in which the two ends of the complex come within a few nanometers of each other, and that the loop region is required for this tight bending.
evidence: This is a conclusion based on the FRET data for the loop deletion mutant.

claim: The Ndc80 complex is commonly drawn as a rigid rod containing a single, distinct hinge point that coincides with the loop region.
source: The Ndc80 complex is commonly drawn as a rigid rod containing a single, distinct hinge point that coincides with the loop region, which is located roughly 20 nm from the Ndc80/Nuf2 end and 40 nm from the Spc24/Spc25 end of the complex (Wang et al., 2008).
evidence: This is a statement about how the Ndc80 complex is typically represented, supported by citation.

claim: The loop region is located roughly 20 nm from the Ndc80/Nuf2 end and 40 nm from the Spc24/Spc25 end of the complex.
source: The Ndc80 complex is commonly drawn as a rigid rod containing a single, distinct hinge point that coincides with the loop region, which is located roughly 20 nm from the Ndc80/Nuf2 end and 40 nm from the Spc24/Spc25 end of the complex (Wang et al., 2008).
evidence: This claim is supported by citation to a previous study.

claim: A simple hinging about the loop region would not bring the two ends of the Ndc80 complex close enough together to explain the high FRET values observed.
source: Given these distances, however, a simple hinging about the loop region would not bring the two ends close enough together to explain the high FRET values we observed (Wang et al., 2008).
evidence: This is an inference based on geometric considerations and the FRET data.

claim: Additional sites of flexibility must exist within the Ndc80 complex.
source: Thus, additional sites of flexibility must exist within the complex.
evidence: This is an inference based on the observation that hinging at the loop alone cannot explain the high FRET.

claim: Flexibility at the junction between the calponin homology domains and the hairpin/coiled coil region has been suggested based on different configurations of this region in crystal structures.
source: Flexibility at the junction between the calponin homology domains and the hairpin/coiled coil region has been suggested based on the different configurations of this region in crystal structures (Valverde et al., 2016; Ciferri et al., 2008).
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to previous structural studies.

claim: Additional hinging at the junction between the calponin homology domains and the hairpin/coiled coil region might be sufficient to bring the two ends of the Ndc80 complex close enough to explain the high FRET.
source: Additional hinging at this second region might be sufficient to bring the two ends close enough to explain the high FRET.
evidence: This is a speculative explanation for how the Ndc80 complex achieves tight bending.

claim: Tight bending of the Ndc80 complex is important for its function in vivo.
source: Tight bending of the Ndc80 complex is important for its function in vivo (Tien et al., 2014) and our observations now show that this conformation is auto-inhibited.
evidence: This claim is supported by citation to a previous study.

claim: Auto-inhibition of the Ndc80 complex might prevent newly expressed Ndc80 complexes from interacting with microtubules prematurely, before they are anchored at a kinetochore.
source: One attractive possibility is that it might prevent newly expressed Ndc80 complexes from interacting with microtubules prematurely, before the Ndc80 complexes are anchored at a kinetochore, thereby avoiding delay or potentially persistent mis-localization.
evidence: This is a speculative explanation for the physiological role of auto-inhibition.

claim: Auto-inhibition might ensure stepwise assembly of the outer kinetochore.
source: Another, not mutually exclusive idea is that auto-inhibition might ensure stepwise assembly of the outer kinetochore.
evidence: This is a speculative explanation for the physiological role of auto-inhibition.

claim: Kinetochores are thought to assemble hierarchically, with the inner-most components assembling first and then outer components building sequentially upon them.
source: Kinetochores are thought to assemble hierarchically, with the inner-most components assembling first and then outer components building sequentially upon them, according to their spatial arrangement (Musacchio and Desai, 2017).
evidence: This claim is supported by citation to a previous review.

claim: Binding of MIND to its kinetochore receptors, Ame1 and Mif2, is prevented by auto-inhibition until MIND binds a nascent kinetochore, where its auto-inhibition can be relieved by Aurora phosphorylation.
source: Previous work shows that binding of MIND to its kinetochore receptors, Ame1 and Mif2, is prevented by auto-inhibition, presumably until MIND binds a nascent kinetochore, where its auto-inhibition can be relieved by Aurora phosphorylation.
evidence: This is a statement about previous work on MIND auto-inhibition, drawing from established knowledge.

claim: The auto-inhibition of Ndc80 complex might prevent it from recruiting the Dam1 complex until it is bound to kinetochore-anchored MIND.
source: Similarly, the auto-inhibition of Ndc80 complex might prevent it from recruiting the Dam1 complex until it is bound to kinetochore-anchored MIND.
evidence: This is a speculative extension of the auto-inhibition mechanism to Dam1 recruitment.

claim: Sequential relief of auto-inhibition might be a general mechanism that encodes stepwise construction at various sites within the kinetochore.
source: Sequential relief of auto-inhibition might be a general mechanism that encodes stepwise construction at various sites within the kinetochore (Dimitrova et al., 2016; Petrovic et al., 2016).
evidence: This is a speculative generalization supported by citations to previous studies.

claim: Some Ndc80 complex is localized to kinetochores independently of the MIND complex and anchored instead via Cnn1/CENP-T.
source: Some Ndc80 complex is localized to kinetochores independently of the MIND complex and anchored instead via Cnn1/CENP-T (Malvezzi et al., 2013).
evidence: This claim is supported by citation to a previous study.

claim: If some kinetochore-anchored Ndc80 complexes can adopt the tightly bent state, then their conformation might be sensitive to kinetochore tension.
source: If some kinetochore-anchored Ndc80 complexes can adopt the tightly bent state, then their conformation might be sensitive to kinetochore tension, potentially contributing to the mechanosensory feedback mechanisms that are thought to control error correction and checkpoint signaling at kinetochores.
evidence: This is a speculative proposal about the potential role of conformational changes in mechanosensing.
